title: What if every lie summons a screaming mirror?
captions: I learn the truth every time I lie. #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #mirrors #lies
The danger closes in as my reflection gets louder. #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #survival #tension
Do I betray myself to save the world? #storytime #fyp #foryou #drama #moral #verdict
parts: [[DAY 1 · 07:13]] I watch my own reflection split and hear it scream, “You’re lying!” My pulse spikes. The mirror fogs, but the words stay sharp. I—MIA—realize every lie summons a scream from that glass, a future echo of truth. [[RULE 1 · NEVER LIE]] I clamp my tongue. I can’t even whisper “I’m fine” without the mirror shrieking. The tiles vibrate with the sound. [[RULE 2 · ONLY SPEAK FACTS]] I force facts out. “I’m awake. I’m alone. The mirror is cracked.” The scream drops to a hiss. A low hum drifts from behind the door. [[3 MINUTES LEFT]] The building’s alarm screams, a siren tearing the air. I bolt to the window, see a red drone hovering, its camera whirring like a beetle. My reflection’s eyes flare crimson, then dim. A cold voice crackles: “Mia, thirty seconds until the cascade starts.” I freeze, breath shallow, as the drone’s beam sweeps the hallway. The mirror shatters, a jagged scream erupts, and a dark shape darts through the broken glass. My heart hammers. A metallic click echoes behind me—something is turning the lock. I spin, and a hand slams onto the knob just as the part cuts.

[[DAY 3 · 22:47]] The city is in blackout, sirens silent, but the mirror’s screams still echo whenever I speak. I’ve survived two days by following the rules, but the drone never left. [[RULE 3 · HIDE IN SHADOWS]] I retreat to the abandoned subway station, lights flickering. The air smells of rust and stale water. [[RULE 4 · NEVER LOOK BACK]] I set up a makeshift camp, covering the mirror with a tarp. The drone hovers above, its red eye pulsing like a heartbeat. A voice crackles again, softer this time: “Mia, I’m you. From the future. We need to stop the crash.” I bite my lip, doubt flooding me. The tarp rustles as a cold wind sneaks through the tunnels. I hear footsteps echoing, far and fast, getting closer. [[5 MINUTES LEFT]] My breath fogs on the cold concrete. A shadow slides past the entrance, a figure in a hazmat suit, holding a metal rod that glints. I clutch the tarp, ready to pull it down. The drone drops a small box onto the platform, beeping. I open it, see a USB drive labeled “EVIDENCE.” My reflection in the broken mirror flashes a frantic warning, “Don’t trust them!” I hear the suit’s wearer whisper, “We’re almost there.” The part stops as I reach for the drive.

[[DAY 7 · 03:12]] The suit‑clad figure hands me the USB. “This will stop the cascade,” they hiss. I plug it into the cracked mirror’s frame. A video plays: a massive oil tanker, years ago, crashed because I signed off on faulty safety checks. The accident killed thousands, set off a chain reaction that now threatens the entire coast. My future self appears on screen, older, eyes haunted, screaming, “Confess! The only way to stop the next crash is to own up now!” The mirror shatters, and the drone spirals down, its red eye dimming. I stare at the reflection of my older self, trembling. The voice of the future self fades, leaving a single line on the screen: “Your truth will reset the timeline.” I realize the only way to save millions is to confess the crime I buried, to become the scapegoat. The suit drops a badge that reads “EXPOSED.” Outside, sirens finally wail, lights flare, and a massive wave looms on the horizon, its crest glowing with the same red as the drone. I stand at the edge, the mirror’s broken pieces glittering like shards of destiny. I turn to the camera, breath ragged, and ask: “Would you betray yourself to save the world, or trust a future that might be lying?”

premise.hook: What if every time I told a lie, my reflection screamed the truth at me?
premise.twist: The narrator discovers their reflection is a future version trying to prevent a catastrophic accident, and the only way to stop it is to confess a hidden crime that caused the accident in the first place.
premise.debate: The community will argue if self‑incrimination is worth saving countless lives, and whether the future self’s warnings are trustworthy.
